items.headline: Oct CPI HOT — headline +0.4% m/m (vs +0.3% fcst, prev +0.6%), core +0.3% (vs +0.2%, prev +0.3%) — core hits Waller's 50bp trigger exactly; no y/y published (Oct 2025 data gap). Dec hike fully priced; the question is now 25bp vs 50bp
Dollar jumps on the hot CPI — DXY ~101.9 (+0.36%, Investing.com ~08:37 ET); USD strongest vs AUD (+0.72%), least vs CAD (+0.30%); EUR/USD 1.1184, GBP/USD 1.3395, USD/JPY 158.40

Waller turns CPI into a 25bp-vs-50bp test: +25bp in Dec even if Oct CPI cools; 50bp if core prints ~0.3% or higher — 'hiking only 25bp would put our credibility at risk'. Dec hike now fully priced (~95.6-99% CME FedWatch), up from ~82% Mon; 2Y +6bp to ~4.61%
Brent falls below $90 for the first time since Aug ($89.92-90.2, -2.5-2.9%) as Trump says the Iran war is 'effectively over' and holds off new strikes; WTI ~$84.6-84.7 (-2.4-2.6%)
Dollar steadies into Oct CPI (7:30am CT, fcst +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%, no y/y — BLS publishes no annual rate); DXY ~101.7, EUR/USD ~1.1220, GBP/USD ~1.3425, USD/JPY ~158.1 after Waller's lift
Gold slips below $4,100 (~$4,097) as Waller's hawkish turn firms the dollar; silver ~$53.27
BoE's Lombardelli 'wouldn't rule out' a December rate hike (Guardian); sterling gives back its 1.3459 London high to ~1.3425 on Waller's dollar lift

BoJ Summary of Opinions turns hawkish: several members want faster hikes toward neutral, 'without becoming overly cautious'; one sees neutral 'considerably above 1%' — Dec hike to 1.50% stays ~80% priced; USD/JPY ~157.98
China Oct trade: surplus $105.3B misses ($126.5B fcst) as imports surge +41.6% y/y (vs +32% exp); exports +35.2% beat — cumulative surplus tops $1T for a second straight year; no FX leg (AUD ~$0.692)

Dollar holds firm in Asia (DXY ~101.6) ahead of US Oct CPI (7:30am CT, fcst +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%, no y/y); Dec Fed hike ~80% (rate-futures) — holding ~80-82% after payrolls; Cleveland Fed nowcast +0.24% headline / +0.21% core
Brent ~$91.44, WTI ~$85.72 in Asia — down ~1% more after Monday's ~5% slide as the Iran premium keeps unwinding; S&P +2.35% Mon, Nasdaq +2.7% as the AI rout pauses

items.headline: NY Fed Oct survey: inflation expectations flat at 3.9% (1y) / 3.3% (3y) / 3.0% (5y) — still above target; jobless-rate expectations hit the highest since April 2020
Dollar gives back Friday's payrolls jump at the NY close — DXY ~101.84 (-0.48%), EUR/USD ~1.1204, GBP/USD ~1.3415, USD/JPY ~158.01; NZD +1.56% to $0.5616 leads as risk rebounds
Dec Fed hike ~82% (CME FedWatch via Reuters) into Tuesday's Oct CPI (7:30am CT, fcst +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%, no y/y) — up from ~81% in the London morning
Brent $94.99 (-3.4%), WTI ~$87.20 (-4.0%) as Iran de-escalation hopes build — Qatar PM meets Trump at the White House; Doha denied the Hormuz-reopening report, but oil kept falling

items.headline: Gold ~$4,126 (+1.4%) as softer oil eases inflation worries, into Tuesday's US CPI; silver ~$52.65
$58B 3Y auction tails 0.5bp — biggest tail since May; BTC 2.53 weakest of 2026, indirects 55.5% (soft foreign demand), directs record 35.0%

Bailey in Zurich: AI an early positive supply shock for the UK (nearly a fifth of GDP growth since early 2026); warns of an 'AI asset price bubble'; stresses central-bank independence — no new December steer
China Oct CPI cools to 0.7% y/y (vs 0.8% fcst) as PPI jumps to 5.7% (vs 5.3%), a four-year high — the CPI–PPI gap widens to ~5pp; core CPI eases to 0.8%
Japan spent a record $50bn in a single day (Jul 30) defending the yen, MoF data confirms — ~$97bn across Jul–Aug, incl. the first joint intervention with the US since 1998; USD/JPY ~158.3

Drone strike halts Iraq's Khor Mor gas field Sun night — LPG tank hit, fire doused, production suspended, ~2.8 GW of Kurdish power out; no casualties, no claim, no restart timeline (Dana Gas / Reuters)
Kiwi strongest overnight (+0.4–0.7%, NZD/USD ~0.5557–0.5585) as the NZ election leaves Luxon's coalition a paper-thin 67-seat majority; official result Nov 27
Risk rebounds: Nasdaq leads Wall St higher after last week's AI rout, VIX ~22.9 (-10.6%); Trump meets Qatar PM at the White House as Iran talks run on

items.headline: US wholesale inventories Sep revised up to +0.7% (from +0.6% advance), sales +2.8% — AI-linked electrical goods +2.5%, petroleum +10.6%
